bullets.title: NVDA CEO Jensen Huang resigns amid China spy scandal, triggering sector rotation
bullets.body: Jensen Huang resigned as NVIDIA CEO following reports of an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset (Alice Huang/Megaspeed), triggering a DOJ probe, congressional scrutiny, and multiple sell-side downgrades. The stock fell 10–17% intraday at various points during the week, closing down ~33% from its early-October peak. The board named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO; Ian Buck is the leading internal successor candidate. Key risks: no formal succession plan, potential tightening of China chip export controls (MATCH Act, AI OVERWATCH Act, Remote Access Security Act), and uncertainty over NVDA's ecosystem financing commitments (~$164B). AMD and AVGO were the primary beneficiaries, each gaining ~15–19% over the week.

bullets.title: October CPI hotter than expected; Fed pricing 3+ hikes through Sep 2027
bullets.body: October core CPI printed +0.30% m/m (third consecutive hot print), headline +0.35%, with 59% of core components rising >3% annualized. Core PCE tracking 0.29–0.35% for October. The Fed is now expected to hike 25bp in December with January increasingly live; markets are pricing ~85bp of additional hikes through end-2027. Fed Governor Waller flagged potential for 50bp in December if inflation remains near 0.3%. JPMorgan, Goldman, and BofA all added a third hike (March 2027) to their base cases, with terminal rate expected at 4.5–4.75%.

bullets.title: S&P 500 +0.2% w/w; NDX bounced ~3.4% mid-week on AI trade revival, breadth fragile
bullets.body: The S&P 500 finished the week ending Nov 13 up only +0.2% (+10.5% YTD) while the NDX rallied ~3.4% led by semis (+8%) and AI infrastructure names. Despite the bounce, only ~37–63% of NASDAQ/Russell 3000 stocks remained above their 200-day MAs, and credit spreads failed to confirm the equity rally. QQQ briefly broke below its 200-day MA. OPCO and 22V noted sentiment at multi-month lows (Investors Intelligence bull/bear ratio fell to 1.5, lowest since April 2026), creating oversold conditions but cautioning that breadth is too narrow to sustain a year-end rally.

bullets.title: AI capex intact in 2027 but 2028 faces ~5GW US project delays and down-cycle risk
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley, JPMorgan, and Goldman all concluded that the midterm election outcome delays—not cancels—approximately 20% of US data center projects from 2028 to 2029, primarily in Texas and Ohio. Hyperscaler capex forecasts remain unchanged at $1.6T/1.8T for 2027/2028. Data centers are more than 30% short of powered capacity through 2028. The 2028 supply chain, however, faces traditional down-cycle risk (flatter orders, margin normalization). CoreWeave's Q3 results (beat/raise, $132.5B backlog, capacity sold out through 2027, <$5B parent capital needed) were cited as the clearest proof of ongoing demand.

bullets.title: Semis cycle debate intensifies: Evercore downgrades cycle; SOX positioning at record lows
bullets.body: Evercore published a detailed semi ChartGPT note arguing semis are growth-cyclicals where P/E compression occurs at successively lower levels as earnings peak. MU P/E fell to 3.6x from 18x and NVDA to 11x from 67x in prior cycles; the note targets NVDA at 8x P/E. Hedge fund net exposure to semis fell 67% from YTD highs to its lowest since September 2025, with six consecutive weeks of selling (a record streak). However, 70% of SOX constituents triggered DeMark buy signals and retail dip-buying was extreme (retail bought $1.6B NVDA on Thursday, the largest ever single-day retail inflow for a single name).

bullets.title: Anthropic IPO launches at $70–78/share (~$1.3T valuation); $26B concurrent private placement
bullets.body: Anthropic filed an amended S-1 offering 825M Class A shares at $70–78/sh (down from earlier $1.5–2T expectations), implying a $917B–$1.4T fully-diluted valuation. The deal was reportedly 6x oversubscribed with $10–15B in index-tracking demand expected in the first four weeks post-listing (ticker: ANT, NASDAQ). A concurrent $26B private placement was committed by AMD, AVGO, GOOGL, MU, MSFT, NVDA, and TSMC. Anthropic's ARR stood at ~$81B as of Oct 31, though 2027 revenue targets of $130B appear aggressive. Pricing was set for Nov 18, trading Nov 19.

bullets.title: Fed turning hawkish: 'immaculate disinflation' thesis officially abandoned
bullets.body: JPMorgan's Global Data Watch titled 'Losing my religion' declared an end to the 'magical thinking' about growth-and-lower-inflation. Global core inflation rebounded to 3.4% annualized through October. Fed communications pivoted away from patient disinflation dogma; December hike likely, with multiple hikes in 2026/2027. Core PPI and consumer import prices rose at 5.5% and 3.3% annualized. The key 2027 risk per JPM: a shift from growth-centric Fed to one committed to price stability even at the cost of weaker growth. NY Fed President Williams (Troika member) noted inflation is 'far too high' and the FOMC agreed to December hike as part of a deal to limit dissents.

bullets.title: 10-year yields back to 5.15%; S&P 500 forward P/E de-rated from 23.2x to 18.2x
bullets.body: US 2-year yields rose ~37bp week-over-week (largest weekly move in two years), 10-year yields hit 5.15%, and mortgage rates touched their highest since 2000. The S&P 500 forward P/E de-rated from 23.2x to 18.2x. Fed pricing implies ~3.5 more hikes by September 2027. JPM noted macro systematic strategies had ~$20B of US equity supply remaining for the following week, with ~$60B of potential equity demand over the next month if realized volatility falls to 15.

bullets.title: Growth-to-value rotation extreme: Russell 1K Value outperformed growth by 32% YTM
bullets.body: Jefferies noted Russell 1000 Value outperformed growth by 32% YTM, the widest swing since the dot-com bubble. Value now trades at the 97th percentile of valuation (18.8x 2FY P/E) while growth is at the 48th percentile (19.4x), reversing the historical premium. OPCO's technical team echoed this, noting the Russell 1000 Value's relative RSI at 66 vs. 33 for Russell 1000 Growth. Market leadership shifting from growth/tech to value/defensive/higher-quality businesses; NVDA, AMAT, and KLAC were removed from large-cap buy lists while RSG, COST, BRK/B, PGR, TXN, SPOT added.

bullets.title: US-China chip export controls escalating; MATCH Act now live risk
bullets.body: Jensen Huang's departure materially accelerated the probability of tighter chip export controls. Commerce is finalizing rules blocking Chinese firms from accessing advanced AI chips via remote data centers in seven additional countries (Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, etc.). Congress is advancing three proposals: MATCH Act (highest escalation risk; could trigger Chinese rare earth retaliation), AI OVERWATCH Act (legal chip sales), and Chip Security Act (anti-smuggling). The 'neocloud loophole'—which provides roughly equivalent compute to chip smuggling via offshore cloud access—is targeted for closure. Oracle cancelled a major Tencent compute contract under administration pressure.

bullets.title: Housing market at GFC lows; existing home sales fell 5.5% to 3.75M in October
bullets.body: Existing home sales fell 5.5% m/m to 3.75M annualized units in October, the lowest since 2010 and matching GFC lows. Mortgage rates are at their highest since 2000 (excluding one month in 2023). Median home price grew only 0.4% YoY—the smallest gain since February. Inventories rose to a cycle high of 5.1 months' supply. The housing recovery requires both lower Treasury yields and lower rate volatility. National home prices are forecast roughly flat in 2027.

bullets.title: Data center capex boom peaks 2028/2029; hyperscaler free cash flows turn negative
bullets.body: Multiple macro shops (PSC, Piper Sandler) warned that data center capex contributions to GDP (~2ppts this year) will cool sharply in 2028 and slow significantly in 2029 as announced/planned construction is down 20% and Mag8/Neoclouds cut 2028 spending. Taiwan's tech export growth is peaking in 2026. Goldman noted AI capex now accounts for 41% of S&P 500 total cash use—exceeding shareholder returns for the first time since 2021—while AMZN and GOOGL are experiencing sharp FCF declines and rising debt.

bullets.title: MSFT global Outlook outage (non-cyberattack) highlights AI workflow centrality
bullets.body: Microsoft suffered a 16-hour global Outlook/Teams/Copilot outage caused by a server CPU usage spike from a configuration update—not a cyberattack. Recovery was phased across APAC, Europe, and North America. The incident drove cybersecurity stocks sharply higher (PANW, CRWD, NET +2–4%) and briefly weighed on MSFT stock (-1.5%). MS analyst Adam Wood maintained Overweight, noting the outage highlighted MSFT's central role in enterprise workflows rather than undermining its franchise.

bullets.title: Semi equipment bullish: AMAT beats, 2027 WFE growth >30%, capacity expansion accelerating
bullets.body: Applied Materials beat Q4 EPS ($4.16 vs. $4.06 est.) and guided Q1 revenues to $11.10B (+2.3% above consensus). Management expects 2027 WFE to grow >30%, with AMAT positioned to outperform the market. Advanced Packaging grew +90% YoY driven by HBM demand; Process Control +50% YoY. The company is tracking 20+ fab ramps in CY27 and expects capacity constraints to ease throughout 2027. Its largest customer is now providing rolling 8-quarter forecasts with no order pushouts.

bullets.title: Cisco strong beat/raise; FY27 AI hyperscaler revenue raised to $9B (+100% YoY)
bullets.body: Cisco beat Q1 EPS ($1.40 vs. $1.33 est.) on networking strength, raising FY27 AI revenue guidance to $9B from $7.5B—implying 125% YoY growth and 60% of the $2.5B total revenue raise. FY27 EPS guidance lifted to $5.47–5.53 from $5.05–5.11. Product orders grew +21% (ex-webscale +14%), with security orders up 15% and firewall orders +30%+ for the third consecutive quarter. Gross margin headwinds from hardware mix were offset by operating leverage. The stock faded from initial highs on order deceleration vs. the prior quarter's +35%.

bullets.title: Retail dip-buying in AI names was historically extreme; institutions net sold
bullets.body: Retail investors bought $1.6B of NVDA on Thursday—10x the next-most-bought name and the third-largest single-stock retail inflow since August 2013. NVDA accounted for 61% of all retail net buying for the week. Concurrently, hedge funds net sold US equities for the second straight week, with US Financial sector selling at an 8-month high (99th percentile). Long-only investors rotated out of NVDA into hyperscalers and large-cap tech. Momentum regime shift is re-emerging with AI names moving from the long to the short leg of 3m/6m momentum baskets.

bullets.title: Brent crude fell 20%+ from Oct 30 peak on US-Iran de-escalation; supports non-US equities
bullets.body: Brent crude fell from ~$118/bbl to ~$96/bbl as Trump signaled that further Iran military strikes were 'highly unlikely' and preliminary US-Iran nuclear deal talks progressed. The IEA reported the oil market returned to surplus in October. Lower oil is modestly disinflationary, reduces energy-driven rate pressure, and—per Jefferies—supports non-US equity outperformance. Physical crude markets remain fragile given Middle East geopolitics and Iraq/Saudi supply dynamics.

bullets.title: Global REITs outperformed tech by 14.9ppts during this AI-sector drawdown
bullets.body: The FTSE EPRA Nareit Developed Index returned +6.6% month-to-date vs. the S&P 500 IT Index -16.5%. Historically, global REITs have outperformed tech by 14.9ppts during IT sector drawdowns >10% since 1990. Within REITs, self-storage and Hong Kong led; US apartment new-lease rents accelerated in October, particularly in coastal markets; healthcare REIT fundamentals are broadening; and net lease REITs are active acquirers on expanding cap rates. Data center REITs specifically rallied on the AI buildout narrative despite near-term permitting headwinds.

bullets.title: SPCX-TSLA merger progressing; SpaceX planning $74B in Arizona and Texas data center campuses
bullets.body: Multiple sources noted SpaceX and Tesla are progressing toward a merger announcement expected December 2026 or early 2027. Separately, SpaceX is planning $50B Arizona and $24B Texas supercomputing campus investments. SpaceX also acquired $8B of nationwide 800 MHz spectrum from Grain Management (FCC filing accepted), accelerating its path as a fifth US wireless competitor. Tower stocks (AMT, CCI, SBAC) rallied on SpaceX network buildout expectations.

bullets.title: ChatGPT Ads reached $1B ARR with 10K advertisers; Pinterest faces biggest share loss
bullets.body: A Roth survey found OpenAI's ChatGPT Ads hit ~$1B annualized run rate by August 2026, growing from ~600 to 10,000+ advertisers in seven months. However, only 11% of agencies are buying ChatGPT ads, and ROI perception is rated 'middling'—in line with Pinterest/Nextdoor, below Google/Instagram/TikTok. Pinterest was identified as the clearest share donor, with more agencies planning to cut vs. add spend there in 2026–2027. The key open question is whether ChatGPT spend represents new money or reallocation from Google, Meta, and Amazon.
